sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case are that:
The land bearing Sy.No.70/2 measuring to an extent of 1089 sq. feet of Bommanahalli village, Beguru Hobli, Bangalore South Taluka has been acquired for the purpose of widening of NH-7.
Preliminary notification was issued on 14.12.1994.
Final notification has published in the Gazette on 20.06.1996.
The award has been passed on 31.01.1997.
The LAO has fixed the compensation at Rs.45/- per sq. feet.
Being aggrieved by the said compensation, the claimant had filed an application under Section 18(1) of the L.A. Act to send the reference to the Court.
Accordingly, the LAO has sent the reference to this Court.

.3. On receipt of the reference, the claimant has entered appearance and filed claim statement stating that he was the absolute owner in lawful possession and enjoyment of immovable property bearing gramathana khatha/HSL N.93/1, LAC No.84/2001 comprised in old Sy. No.70/2, situated at Bommanahalli village, Begur Hobli, Bangalore South Taluka, consisting of land and building measuring 1089 sq. feet was acquired for the purpose of widening of National Highway No.7.

It is stated that the sital value of the property is not valued properly, the property situated at the centre of the village in the National Highway No.7, it is a gramathana property, it is center for all business establishments as such the value of market value as to be valued on the basis of commercial value of the site.
It is stated that the market value is fixed on assumption and presumption without enquiring and ascertaining.
Hence, the same is not acceptable to the claimant.
The correct market value of the property of the claimant is Rs.1,000/- per sq. feet, the amount paid by this authority is far below the market value.
.4. It is stated that for the purpose of widening of National Highway No.7 as an additional acquisition has taken more than 1,300 sq. feet from the property of the claimant.
Whereas the award is made only for 1,089 sq. feet.
The value of the building was also not valued properly.
In accordance L.A.C. No. 84/2001 with the correct measurement and the value of the building is also to be adjudicated and the award amount has to be paid to the claimant.
It is stated that the building constructed on the property of the claimant is of RCC building "A" class constructions consisting of ground floor and 1 st floor.
The building was being used for commercial establishments.

The value being taken for the assessment of value of the building per sq. meter is far below and the classification taken into consideration for valuing the building is totally not correct and the same is not acceptable to the claimant.
It is stated that at the time of passing the award the authority has not considered the proper market value of the site and the building.
Hence, prayed for enhancement of compensation.
.5. The respondent No.2 has filed objections stating that the respondent No.2 i.e., National Highways Authority of India was constituted by an Act of Parliament.
It is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of National Highways entrusted to it and for matter connected or incidental thereto.

The Deputy Commissioner, Bangalore for purpose of widening of Bangalore Hosuru Section of NH-7 issued preliminary notification was published on 14 th LAC No.84/2001 December 1994 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

The respondent Vajramuniyappa B.N vs ) The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60842343/
2 No.1 vide award bearing No.LAQ/BLR/13/94-95 dated 31st January 1997 determined the market value of non-agricultural lands at Rs.45/- per sq. feet.
In order to determine the market value, the respondent No.1 had obtained the sale statistics and guidance value of agricultural lands for the relevant period of the said village.

The respondent No.1 decided to award compensation at the rate of Rs.45/- per sq. feet along with statutory benefits in accordance with LA Act as well as the compensation for the structures and malkies in the subject lands which is determined as per the report of the valuators.
That the instant claim petition filed by the claimant is barred by time.
That as per proviso the Sub Section (2)
, the claimant has to make the application before the Deputy Commissioner within 90 days from the date of receipt of the award notice.
The claimant for the reasons best known to him has not pleaded that the application was in time and as to when he received the notice.

Further, on perusal of the entire application filed under Section 18(1) of the LA Act the claimant has not L.A.C. No. 84/2001 disclosed any cogent reason in order to substantiate the delay and hence, the claim petition is hopelessly barred by limitation.
The claimant has not produced an iota of documents supporting the same.
The claimant has failed to produce documentary documents in order to show this Court in what way the market value determined is less.
In the absence of the same, the claimant is not entitled for any relief.
The claimant has not produced a single scratch of proof to show that the market value as on the date of publication of the preliminary notification was Rs.1,000/- per sq. feet.

It is pertinent to note that the claimant on one hand claims that no compensation has been paid for the buildings and on the other hand claims that the proper compensation has been disbursed, which shows that he has blown both hot and cold at the same point in time.

Further, the spot inspection was conducted on 05.12.1996 and the building acquired had been duly valuated by the Chief Executive Engineer and as per the reports, the compensation had been determined and paid to the claimant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

.6. In order to substantiate the case, claimant has been examined as PW.1 and has got marked documents at Ex.P.1to Ex.P.4.
.7.
Heard the arguments.

.8. The following points that arise for my consideration are:
1. Whether the reference is in time?
2. Whether the compensation awarded by the L.A.O., to the claimant is in- adequate?
3. What Order or Award?

.9. My findings on the above points are as follows:-
 Point No.1 : In the affirmative,
 Point No.2 : Partly in the affirmative,
Point No.3 : As per the final order for the Vajramuniyappa B.N vs ) The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60842343/

 R E A S ON S
.10. Point No.1:- The award has been passed on 30.08.1997.
The claimant has filed the application before the LAO on 26.11.1997 as per Ex.P.1.
The 19 particulars discloses that the notice has been served on 09.09.1997.
The L.A.C. No. 84/2001 application is filed by the claimant within 90 days.
So, the application is in time.
In the evidence it is elicited from the claimant that he has received the compensation on 16.09.1995.
The respondent has not lead any evidence.

There appears to be typographical mistake in the date as award passed on 30.08.1997.
.11.
The LAO has sent the reference on 12.02.1998.
The LAO has sent the reference within 3 years 90 days from the date of receipt of the application and so, the reference sent by the LAO is in time.
Hence, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative.
.12. Point No.2:

The respondent No.1 has acquired the property bearing gramathana / CMC/ BBMP khatha No. 93/1 comprised in Sy. No.70/2 of Bommanahalli village belonging to the claimant under preliminary notification dated 14..12.1994.
The LAO has fixed the compensation of Rs.45/- per sq. feet.
Not being satisfied with the said amount, the claimant has filed the application under Section 18 of LA Act seeking for enhancement of compensation.
.13. The claimant has been examined as PW.1.

He has stated that the respondent No.1 has passed the award at the LAC No.84/2001 rate of Rs.45/- per sq. feet without any basis; that the respondent No.1 failed to assess the market value on the basis of nature of the property, potentiality of the property, situation and use of the land and building.

The property in question is situated at Hosuru - Bangalore main road NH-7 coming under Bommanahalli BBMP ward No. 174, 8.5 kms distance from the city centre and it was a prime place; that it was a commercial property in nature and converted land.
It has got high potential value; that surrounding the property well developed with large, medium and small scale industries, hotels, bus terminals schools and colleges etc.
That it is in the place almost bazaar street, where number of shops have established either side of the NH-7.

Adjoining on the east BDA had formed residential layout called HSR layout acquiring lands of Bommanahalli village; that R.K. steel, BSNL Exchange office, post office, Thirumala hospital,
Garment factories, residential apartments and other number of commercial establishment are located within the radious of the property.

Further transport office, BBMP office, number of nationalized banks, car show rooms are in existence and L.A.C. No. 84/2001 the said factors were not considered by the respondent No.1 while passing the award.

.14. PW.1 has stated that the property in question is not a revenue agricultural property, it is within the gramathana limits of Bommanahalli BBMP ward No.174, surrounded by commercial buildings.

sentences.text: There is no sale or purchase of land on either side of road since several decades the land and property owners are using for themselves as commercial properties.

PW.1 has stated that the respondent No.1 failed to assess the value in terms of market value for commercial properties at 40% has to be added in the CMC gramathana and BBMP limits, abutting to National Highways, 50%
more value shall be added while assessing the valuation by the respondent No.1.
PW.1 has stated that the respondent No.1 has failed to assess the market value of the land.
In support of his contention that the property is in developed area.
The claimant has not produced any documentary evidence nor he has produced the guidance value.
.15. PW.1 has relied upon the judgment and award passed in LAC No.75/2003 as per Ex.P.3 and 4.
From the judgment, it is seen that It is stated that in respect of the LAC No.84/2001 property in Khaneshumari No.104/1 situated at Bommanahalli gramathana, Begur village.
Preliminary notification was issued on 15.05.1995 and final notification was issued on 16.11.1996.
The award was passed on 19.05.1997.
In the said case, the respondent No.1 has fixed the market value of acquired property at Rs.45/- per sq. feet.
This Court had held that the claimants are entitled for market value of the acquired property at the rate of Rs. 200/- per sq. feet instead of Rs.45/- per sq. feet.
.16. During cross examination PW.1 has stated that for the first time he has received the award notice in the year 1997.
He has stated that his property consists of 2 floors.
He admits that he has received the compensation amount on 16.09.1995.
When it is suggested that in Sy. No.70/2, 1.5 guntas was acquired, the claimant has stated that it is first acquisition.
The present acquisition is 1 gunta.
He has stated that the notification has been issued in the year 1994.

PW.1 has stated that as per the market value of neighbouring lands, 40% has to be given for commercial property and 50%
for lands situated adjacent to the National Highways.
The respondents have not chosen to lead any evidence.
From the General Award, it is seen that the LAO called for the sales statistics of 3 years prior to the notification and has arrived at an average sale at Rs.42.25.
He has stated that in LAQ/BLR/70/1994-95, the market value has been fixed at Rs.45/- per sq. feet.
So, he comes to the conclusion that in this case also the market value has to be fixed at Rs.45/- per sq. feet.
.18. The claimant has not produced any sales statistics for the relevant period.
So, the market value cannot be fixed on the basis of sales statistics method.
Like-wise, the claimant has also not produced any documents with regard to the Income derived from the property.
So, this Court cannot fix the market value based on the capitalization method.

The claimant has stated that his land is situated in a commercial area and so, the market value has to be determined at 40% more than guidance value as the land is situated in commercial area and 50% has to be added a land is situated on the National Highways.
He has not produced any guidance value.
This Court cannot determine the market value on the LAC No.84/2001 basis of the guidance value.

The claimant has however relied upon the judgment of this Court in LAC No.75/2003.
.19.
Now law is well settled that the decided judgment of any of the reference Court can be relied upon in order to come to just and fair conclusion in-respect of fixing just and fair compensation.

In this regard, I would like to bank upon the following decisions reported in AIR 2003 Supreme Court Vajramuniyappa B.N vs ) The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60842343/
5 4382 wherein it is held as under:
" (A) Land Acquisition Act (1 of 1894), S2- Compensation-Determination of, on basis of earlier judgments-Plea that High Court erred in not taking sale instances into account while fixing compensation- Compensation already fixed by High Court in earlier proceedings and Supreme Court in one such proceeding has already approved rate fixed-Best method would be to look at the earlier judgments and Awards and not sale instances - High Court cannot be faulted for having fixed compensation on the basis of earlier judgments" & one more decision which came to be reported in 2005(4) KCCR short notes L.A.C. No. 84/2001 264 (General Manager, ONGC V/s Sendhabal Vastram Patel &
others), which is as under:
" Land Acquisition Act, 1894, Section 18 - market value - the best method for determining market value of acquired land is the amount which a willing purchaser of the land would pay to the owner of the land as may be evidenced by deeds of sale - in the absence of any direct evidence on the said point, the Court may take recourse to other methods, viz., judgments and awards passed in-respect of acquisitions of lands made in the same village and/or neighbouring villages.

sentences.text: The Reference Court has to apply the comparable sales method and also the situation of the land, which is to be appreciated upon considering the question as to whether acquired land is similar to any land sold in the vicinity".
The said decision applies to the case on hand.
The land in Ex.P.3 is situated in Bommanahalli gramathana.
The preliminary notification in the said case has been issued on LAC No.84/2001 15.05.1995.
The land has been acquired for the purpose of widening of NH-7.

In the present case,
the land is situated in Bommanahalli village and though it is survey number land, it is treated as NAK at the time of awarding compensation.
The acquisition is for the purpose of widening of NH-7 road.
The land in question and the land in Ex.P.3 has been acquired for the same purpose and situation of the land is also the same.
However, the preliminary notification in the present case has been issued on 14.12.1994, whereas, preliminary notification in Ex.P.3 has been issued on 15.03.1995.
There is a difference of 6 months in the notification.
The learned counsel for the respondent has argued that preliminary notification in Ex.P.3 is subsequent to the preliminary notification in the present case.
The judgment in Ex.P.3 cannot be relied upon.

.20. In AIR 2012 SCC 446 (Chandrashekar and others Vs. LAO and another), the Hon'ble Supreme Court had observed that:
"Deescalation - keeping in view fact that land prices are on rise throughout country,
deduction of 10% under head of de-escalation would be justified.

sentences.text:
Relying upon the above judgment our Hon'ble Court in MFA No.6329/2014 A.C.
Gurumurthy dead by Lrs Vs. Special Land Acquisition Officer has held that Preliminary Notification was issued in the present case on 16.11.1988 Gazette on 23.03.1989 while preliminary notification in MFA No.7462/2009 was issued on 17.09.1992 there was difference of 3 years 5 months 24 days between 2 preliminary notification and the same could be rounded of at 3 years 6 months.
The depreciation if calculated at the rate of 10% on Rs.75/- per sq. feet as awarded in MFA No.7462/2009, the compensation could be rounded of at Rs.49/- per sq. feet.
The above principle applies to the case on hand. .21.
The Hon'ble Court in LAC No.75/2003 has re- determined the compensation at Rs.200/- per sq. feet.
If the depreciation of market value is calculated at the rate of 10% on Rs.200/- per sq. feet for 6 months, the market value would be Rs.190/- per sq. feet.
The claimant in this case is entitled LAC No.84/2001 for market value at Rs.190/- per sq. feet with all statutory benefits.
.22. The claimant has sought for enhancement in respect of structures in the claim statement.
However, in his evidence the claimant has not stated with regard to the enhancement of compensation.
He has not produced the valuation report or cost incurred by him with regard to the construction, approved plan pertaining to the building etc.
The claimant has failed to prove with cogent materials that he is entitled for enhanced compensation amount in respect of the structures.
Hence, the LAO award in respect of structures is accepted.

.23. The appreciation of oral and documentary evidence on record, leads to the unmistakable fact that the claimant proves that the market value fixed by the respondent - L.A.O., in-respect of his acquired land, in this case, is unjust, inadequate and on lower side.
Thus, the claimant in this case, is entitled for market value at Rs.190/- per sq. feet with all statutory benefits.
The claimant is entitled for the aforesaid market value of his acquired land and consequently the statutory benefits from the date of publication of preliminary L.A.C. No. 84/2001 notification.
Hence, I answer point No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
.24. Point No.3:
In view of my finding on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The reference made by the of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is partly allowed.

sentences.text:
The claimant is entitled for market value for his acquired land at the rate of Rs. 190/-
per sq.ft. instead of Rs.45/- per acre as awarded by the respondent in respect of Sy.No. 70/2 measuring to an extent of 1089 sq. feet of Bommanahalli village, Beguru Hobli, Bangalore South Taluka.

Further, the claimant is entitled for additional market value under Section 23(1)A of Land Acquisition Act @ 12% p.a. on the enhanced market value of Rs.145/- (Rs.190 - 45) from the date of preliminary LAC No.84/2001 notification till the date of taking possession or the date of award whichever is earlier.
Further, the claimant is entitled for solatium at the rate of 30% p.a. on the enhanced market value of Rs.145/- under Section 23(2) of Land Acquisition Act.

Further, the claimant is entitled for interest at the rate of 9% p.a. on the enhanced market value of Rs.45/-, solatium and additional market value for a period of one year from the date of taking possession of acquired land and further interest @ 15%
p.a. for subsequent years till deposit of entire compensation amount.
The LAO award in respect of structures is confirmed.
The amount already paid by the respondent No.1/SLAO, if any, shall L.A.C. No.
84/2001 be deducted in the enhancement of the market value now awarded.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the JW, transcribed by her, corrected by me and then pronounced in open Court on this the 20 th day of February, 2022.)
(Sheila B.M.), II Addl. City Civil and Sessions & Spl. Judge, Bengaluru.
